description: Make a film, commercial or story video from an idea, script or attached pictures, and write long ones step by step.

offer.reason: offered only when the person asks for a film, movie, episode or long video; adult on their own written screen with video on

author: MaiPai

examples: Make a 40 second film of a paper boat in the rain
Make a short movie about two cats finding a garden
Turn this scene into a film with six shots
Create a 90 second film from this script
Make a cartoon short about a fox and a moonlit forest
Make a 3 minute video about a lighthouse keeper
Write me a sitcom episode about two roommates
I want a feature-length movie about a heist
Make a 30-second commercial for this coffee mug
Use these photos to make an ad for my product
Make a video from these pictures
Yes, that is good, go on

idea.description: The story in the person's own words. Keep their meaning and details.

shots.description: Optional number of shots, from 4 to 12. Set only when the person asks for a number.

seconds.description: Total length in seconds the person asked for. Over 120 starts a production written in steps; ask once if a long one has no length.

look.description: Optional look in plain words, such as 1975 35mm, overcast, muted, or cartoon. Set only when the person asks for a look.

characters.description: Names of saved characters or synths, only when named. Never attached pictures or file names: Home reads those.

go_ahead.description: Set true only when the person asked to skip checking the plan first. Otherwise leave out or set false; the person reviews the plan and presses Go.

faceless.description: a narrated film of pictures with slow zoom and pan, no characters moving

production_id.description: A production being continued, from the earlier result.

approve.description: True, with production_id, only when the person said the last step is good and to go on.

track.description: Optional: one of the person's own saved songs to use as the film's music instead of making one: its music job id (musicJobId of an earlier generate_music result in this chat), a Library file id, or latest for the newest song finished in this chat. Set only when the person asks to use a song they made.
